note: Machine-readable BMAD compatibility manifest. EOS delegates authoring work to BMAD skills; those skills resolve their customization and memory through a PROJECT-LOCAL runtime under `_bmad/`, which is NOT part of EOS and is NOT vendored here. `eos-doctor --deep` reads this file and reports BLOCKED when a mapped skill cannot activate at all, and DEGRADED when it activates only on shipped defaults — so a green doctor can no longer coexist with a failing skill activation, and a working-but-uncustomized setup is not mislabelled as broken. See docs/adr/003-bmad-runtime-boundary.md.

runtime.provider: BMAD Method (installed separately by its own installer, into the project)

scripts.purpose: resolves per-skill customize.toml overrides; every mapped skill calls it on activation
session memory log used by the facilitation skills

executables.name: uv
executables.purpose: runs memlog.py and some skill-local scripts

runtime.absenceBehaviour: DEGRADED, not BLOCKED. Every mapped skill documents a fallback: if `resolve_customization.py` cannot run it resolves the block itself from `{skill-root}/customize.toml`, and "any missing file is skipped". Without this runtime the skills therefore still activate on their shipped defaults; what is lost is PROJECT-LEVEL customization (`_bmad/custom/*.toml` overrides, the module config, session memory). eos-doctor reports that as a warning — calling it BLOCKED would be a false red, the mirror image of the false green this manifest exists to remove.

fallback.policy: EOS never depends on BMAD to make a decision. Every gate, evaluator, transition and router decision in EOS runs with no BMAD installed at all; the skills only make the AUTHORING faster. When a skill is unavailable, `eos next` still names the action, the target gate and the done-when — do the step manually.
